cards.front: Kelly le tiró los pañuelos a Pam.
cards.back: Kelly threw the tissues to Pam.

cards.front: Pam le tiró el paquete de pañuelos a George.
cards.back: Pam threw the packet of tissues to George.

cards.front: George le tiró el paquete de chicles a Fred.
cards.back: George threw the packet of chewing gum to Fred.

cards.front: Pam le devolvió los pañuelos a Kelly tirándoselos.
cards.back: Pam threw the tissues back to Kelly.

cards.front: Ella se los devolvió a ella rápidamente tirándoselos.
cards.back: She threw them back to her quickly.

cards.front: ¿Devolvió Fred los chicles a George tirándoselos?
cards.back: Did Fred throw the chewing gum back to George?

cards.front: Pam le tiró las vendas a Fred.
cards.back: Pam threw Fred the bandages.

cards.front: Él le tiró a Fred unas tijeras y cinta adhesiva.
cards.back: He threw Fred some scissors and some sticky tape.

cards.front: ¿Le tiraste también a Fred una grapadora y unas grapas?
cards.back: Did you throw Fred a stapler and some staples too?

cards.front: James acaba de tirar una piedra a la ventana.
cards.back: James just threw a rock at the window.

cards.front: Él tiró una piedra a la ventana y después le tiró un huevo a Eleanor.
cards.back: He threw a rock at the window and then he threw an egg at Eleanor.

cards.front: Me pregunto por qué Eleanor le tiró su bebida a Pam.
cards.back: I wonder why Eleanor threw her drink at Pam.

cards.front: Eleanor tiró su cóctel a la cara de Pam.
cards.back: Eleanor threw her cocktail in Pam's face.

cards.front: ¿Has oído que Alan tiró su cerveza a la cara de William?
cards.back: Did you hear Alan threw his beer in William's face?

cards.front: Me pregunto por qué Charlotte tiró la empanada a la cara de Kevin. Él le mintió.
cards.back: I wonder why Charlotte threw the pie in Kevin's face. He lied to her.

cards.front: ¿Ha tirado Sheila ese pan mohoso? ¡Es asqueroso!
cards.back: Has Sheila thrown away that mouldy bread? It's revolting!

cards.front: ¿Ha tirado ella esa leche agria también? ¡Es repugnante!
cards.back: Has she thrown away that sour milk too? It's vile!

cards.front: Sí, ella ha tirado la leche agria junto con el pan mohoso.
cards.back: Yes, she's thrown away the sour milk along with the mouldy bread.

cards.front: Mis compañeros de piso todavía no han tirado la basura. ¡Es asqueroso!
cards.back: My flatmates haven't thrown out the rubbish yet. It's revolting!

cards.front: ¡Han tirado todas mis cosas!
cards.back: They've thrown out all my stuff!

cards.front: Perdón, hemos tirado todas tus cosas viejas junto con la basura.
cards.back: Sorry, we've thrown out all your old stuff along with the trash.

cards.front: ¡Han echado a Michael de la discoteca junto con Robert!
cards.back: Michael's been thrown out of the club along with Robert!

cards.front: ¡Ay, dios mío! ¿Por qué les han echado?
cards.back: Oh my God! What have they been thrown out for?

cards.front: ¡Les han echado por bailar en las mesas!
cards.back: They've been thrown out for dancing on the tables!

cards.front: Le han echado a él de la discoteca.
cards.back: They've thrown him out of the club.

cards.front: ¿Por qué le han echado a él de la discoteca?
cards.back: What have they thrown him out of the club for?

cards.front: Le han echado a él por bailar en las mesas.
cards.back: They've thrown him out for dancing on the tables.

cards.front: ¿Han echado ya a ese rarito de marketing?
cards.back: Have they gotten rid of that creep in marketing yet?

cards.front: Han estado intentando echar a su compañera de piso. ¡Es asquerosa!
cards.back: They've been trying to get rid of their flatmate. She's disgusting!

cards.front: Ella ha echado a su novio. ¡Era un rarito!
cards.back: She's gotten rid of her boyfriend. He was a creep!

cards.front: Sé que es tu primer día, pero voy a tirarte a la parte más honda de la piscina.
cards.back: I know it's your first day but I'm going to throw you in at the deep end.

cards.front: Sí que me tiraron a la parte más honda de la piscina.
cards.back: They really threw me in at the deep end.

cards.front: Me tiraron a la parte más honda de la piscina para ver si me hundía o nadaba.
cards.back: They threw me in at the deep end to see if I would sink or swim.

cards.front: Yo sólo digo esto; creo que Jeffrey robó el dinero.
cards.back: I'm just throwing it out there; I think Jeffrey stole the money.

cards.front: Yo sólo digo esto; creo que Helen es guapísima.
cards.back: I'm just throwing it out there; I think Helen is gorgeous.

cards.front: Ahí va esto; creo que Helen ayudó a Jeffrey a robar el dinero.
cards.back: I'm just going to throw this out there; I think Helen helped Jeffrey to steal the money.

cards.front: Hablemos con Helen. A lo mejor ella puede arrojar algo de luz sobre el caso.
cards.back: Let's talk to Helen. Maybe she can throw some light on the case.

cards.front: ¿Puedes arrojar algo de luz sobre la situación, Helen?
cards.back: Can you throw some light on the situation, Helen?

cards.front: Quizás tú puedas arrojar algo de luz sobre lo que ocurrió aquella noche.
cards.back: Maybe you can throw some light on what happened that night.

cards.front: Helen no hablará. Creo que es hora de tirar la toalla.
cards.back: Helen won't talk. I think it's time to throw in the towel.

cards.front: No averiguamos lo que pasó. Tiremos la toalla.
cards.back: We didn't find out what happened. Let's throw in the towel.

cards.front: Estaba a punto de tirar la toalla cuando Helen confesó.
cards.back: I was about to throw in the towel when Helen confessed.

cards.front: ¡Hemos resuelto el caso! ¡Hagamos una fiesta!
cards.back: We solved the case! Let's throw a party!

cards.front: Ahí va esto; ¡hagamos una fiesta en la oficina!
cards.back: I'm just going to throw it out there; let's throw a party in the office!

cards.front: No sé lo que pasó anoche. ¡Hicimos una fiesta enorme!
cards.back: I don't know what happened last night. We threw a huge party!

cards.front: ¡Ponte cualquier cosa, que llegamos tarde!
cards.back: Just throw some clothes on, we're late!

cards.front: Me pongo algo y estoy allí en quince minutos.
cards.back: I'll just throw some clothes on and I'll be there in fifteen minutes.

cards.front: ¡Rápido! Ponte algo. Hay alguien en la puerta.
cards.back: Quick! Throw some clothes on. Someone's at the door.

cards.front: ¡Ponte cualquier cosa, que vamos tarde!
cards.back: Just throw something on, we're running late!

cards.front: ¿Cómo que no sabes qué ponerte? ¡Ponte lo que sea!
cards.back: What do you mean you don't know what to wear? Just throw something on.

cards.front: Hay alguien en la puerta. ¡Rápido! Ponte algo.
cards.back: Someone's at the door. Quick! Throw something on.

cards.front: ¡Venga! Ponte el abrigo y sal a dar un paseo.
cards.back: Come on! Throw your coat on and come out for a walk.

cards.front: ¡Más vale que te abrigues! ¡Ponte el abrigo, está helando!
cards.back: You'd better wrap up! Throw on your coat, it's freezing!

cards.front: ¿Por qué no te pones el abrigo y sales a dar un paseo?
cards.back: Why don't you just throw on your coat and come out for a walk?

cards.front: Está helando, pero estarás bien si te pones la bufanda y los guantes.
cards.back: It's freezing, but you'll be all right if you throw on your scarf and gloves.

cards.front: Hace un frío que pela, pero estarás bien si te pones la bufanda y los guantes.
cards.back: It's freezing cold, but you'll be OK if you throw on your scarf and gloves.

cards.front: ¡Más vale que te abrigues! Ponte la bufanda y los guantes y estarás bien.
cards.back: You'd better wrap up! Throw on your scarf and gloves and you'll be alright.

cards.front: ¿Te apetece un baño? ¡Ponte el bañador y vámonos! (Usa «up for».)
cards.back: Are you up for a swim? Throw on your bathing suit and let's go!

cards.front: ¿Te apetece un baño? Ponte el bañador y vámonos. (Usa «fancy».)
cards.back: Do you fancy a swim? Throw on your bathing suit and let's go!

cards.front: ¿Te apetece ir a la playa? ¡Ponte el bañador y vámonos!
cards.back: Do you fancy going to the beach? Throw on your bathing suit and let's go!

cards.front: ¡Tira p'alante!
cards.back: Get a move on!

cards.front: Vamos tarde. ¡Tira p'alante!
cards.back: We're running late. Get a move on!

cards.front: ¡Tira p'alante! Tenemos que irnos.
cards.back: Get a move on! We have to go.

cards.front: ¡Tira p'atrás!
cards.back: Back up!

cards.front: No te pongas delante de la puerta. ¡Tira p'atrás!
cards.back: Don't stand in front of the door. Back up!

cards.front: No aparques delante de la puerta del jardín. ¡Tira p'atrás!
cards.back: Don't park in front of the garden gate. Back up!

cards.front: Él debe de tener unos cuarenta y muchos años tirando por lo alto.
cards.back: He must be in his late forties at the very most.

cards.front: No estoy de acuerdo. Creo que él debe de tener unos cincuenta y muchos tirando por lo alto.
cards.back: I don't agree. I think he must be in his late fifties at the very most.

cards.front: No estoy de acuerdo con vosotros dos. Él debe de tener unos sesenta y muchos tirando por lo alto.
cards.back: I disagree with both of you. He must be in his late sixties at the very most.

cards.front: Ella debe de tener unos treinta y pocos tirando por lo bajo.
cards.back: She must be in her early thirties at the very least.

cards.front: No estoy de acuerdo. Ella debe de tener unos cuarenta y pocos años tirando por lo bajo.
cards.back: I don't agree. She must be in her early forties at the very least.

cards.front: No estoy de acuerdo con vosotros dos. Ella debe de tener unos cincuenta y pocos años tirando por lo bajo.
cards.back: I disagree with both of you. She must be in her early fifties at the very least.

cards.front: ¿Qué tal? ¿Tirando?
cards.back: How are you? Hanging in there?

cards.front: Sí, tirando.
cards.back: Yeah, hanging in there.

cards.front: ¡Ánimo!
cards.back: Hang in there!

cards.front: ¿Acabas de vomitar? Debe de ser algo que has comido.
cards.back: Did you just throw up? It must be something you ate!

cards.front: ¿Acaba de vomitar ella? ¿Ha sido algo que ha comido?
cards.back: Did she just throw up? Was it something she ate?

cards.front: Vomité, pero no estoy enfermo. Debe de ser algo que he comido.
cards.back: I threw up but I'm not ill. It must be something I ate.

cards.front: Madre mía, creo que voy a devolver.
cards.back: Oh god, I think I'm going to be sick.

cards.front: Madre mía, ¡qué asco! Creo que voy a devolver.
cards.back: Oh god, that's revolting! I think I'm going to be sick.

cards.front: ¡Rápido! ¡Vete al arcén! Creo que voy a vomitar.
cards.back: Quick! Pull over! I think I'm going to be sick.

cards.front: ¿Alguna vez vomitas cuando te mareas en un coche?
cards.back: Do you ever throw up when you get carsick?

cards.front: Sí, siempre vomito cuando me mareo en un coche.
cards.back: Yeah, I always throw up when I get carsick.

cards.front: Siempre tengo que pedirle al conductor que se eche al arcén para poder vomitar.
cards.back: I always have to ask the driver to pull over so I can throw up.

cards.front: La verdad es que el salmón no me sienta bien. Siempre vomito cuando lo tomo.
cards.back: Salmon doesn't really agree with me. I always throw up when I have it.

cards.front: La verdad es que a ella no le sientan bien los mejillones. A veces se pone mala cuando los toma.
cards.back: Mussels don't really agree with her. She sometimes gets sick when she has them.

cards.front: No tomes leche si no te sienta bien. ¡Vomitarás!
cards.back: Don't have any milk if it doesn't agree with you. You'll just throw up!

cards.front: No voy a ponerme malo. ¡Sólo es ardor de estómago!
cards.back: I'm not going to get sick. It's just heartburn!

cards.front: No creo que él vaya a vomitar. Tiene ardor de estómago.
cards.back: I don't think he's going to throw up. He has heartburn.

cards.front: Siempre me da ardor de estómago cuando bebo vino tinto, pero no suelo vomitar.
cards.back: I always get heartburn when I drink red wine but I don't usually throw up.
